subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should this sandbox-specific `sessions_spawn` stall be fixed directly in the Docker/subagent startup path, or folded into the broader sub-agent startup lifecycle contract tracked by #58776?
rationale: Both paths are plausible from source: direct propagation would address this report narrowly, while the open lifecycle work would define a broader first-progress/startup-failed contract that could prevent duplicate fixes.

options.title: Keep Open For Lifecycle Decision
options.body: Treat this as the sandbox-specific reproduction that must remain open until the broader lifecycle boundary and live Docker proof are settled.

options.title: Queue A Narrow Sandbox Fix
options.body: Limit the repair to propagating Docker sandbox startup failures into child session/subagent terminal state without adding broader lifecycle phases.

options.title: Close Into #58776
options.body: Make #58776 the canonical item only if maintainers decide the additive lifecycle contract fully owns the sandboxed Docker startup failure path.

recommendation.title: Keep Open For Lifecycle Decision
recommendation.body: Treat this as the sandbox-specific reproduction that must remain open until the broader lifecycle boundary and live Docker proof are settled.

likelyOwner.reason: The explicit `sessions_spawn` sandbox inheritance behavior and most adjacent subagent/sandbox history route through this owner trail.
